mainTopic: How a thief acquires a stolen item: שינוי קונה and its sources, how the fines are valued, and whether יאוש acquires.
overview: The amud opens by finishing the discussion of אתנן. It shows how בית שמאי and בית הלל read the words "הם" and "גם" in the פסוק, and the word "גם" stays a difficulty for בית הלל. The גמרא then says their argument is only about whether שינוי קונה. Everyone agrees that כפל and ארבעה וחמשה are paid based on the item as it was when stolen. This seems to refute רב, who values those fines at the time of trial. רבא answers by separating a physical change in the animal from a change in its market price. Next, רבה shows that שינוי קונה comes from the פסוק "אשר גזל" and from a משנה. One משנה is about wood made into vessels; the other is about first-shearing wool that was dyed before it was given to the כהן, which makes the owner exempt. רבה then says the owner's יאוש also lets the thief acquire, but he is unsure whether this is דאורייתא, like a found lost item, or only דרבנן because of תקנת השבים. רב יוסף disagrees and holds that יאוש does not acquire at all. He then begins challenging רבה from a משנה about stolen חמץ after פסח, and the challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What בית שמאי learn from the word "הם"
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי use the word "הם" to teach that the offspring of an אתנן animal are not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word "these" comes to teach: these, but not their offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining how בית שמאי read the פסוק of אתנן. They learn from the word "הם" that only the animals themselves are forbidden, not their babies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי already use the word "גם" to include a changed אתנן (for example, wheat that was made into flour) in the איסור. So the word "הם" is free for a different lesson: it leaves out the offspring.

keyTerms.meaning: A payment given to a זונה, which may not be brought as a קרבן
"These": a word in the פסוק that limits the איסור
Their offspring
That is what it comes to teach

phrases.english: "These," but not their offspring
phrases.notes: This is from דברים 23:19, the פסוק about אתנן being disgusting to ה׳.

phrases.english: is what it comes to teach.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the earlier discussion of how בית שמאי use each word of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the word "הם" a different job
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without this, one might think בית שמאי have no use for the word "הם".
steps.terutzMaskana: For בית שמאי, "הם" excludes the offspring of the אתנן.

steps.title: בית הלל learn two lessons from "הם"
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל learn both lessons from the one word "הם": a changed item is not forbidden, and offspring are not forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל? They learn two things from it: these, but not their changed form; these, but not their offspring.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how בית הלל can get both lessons out of the same word "הם".
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל hold that a changed אתנן is permitted. They learn this from "הם", and they say that the same word also leaves out the offspring. One word gives two lessons.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn two things from it
Their changed form
The students of הלל

phrases.english: And בית הלל?
phrases.notes: The hidden question: בית הלל already use "הם" for the changed item, so where do they learn that the offspring are allowed?

phrases.english: Learn two things from it:
"These," but not their changed form;
"these," but not their offspring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from בית שמאי's reading of "הם" to בית הלל's reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How do בית הלל learn the offspring rule if they use "הם" for changed items?

steps.title: What do בית הלל do with "גם"?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what בית הלל learn from the word "גם", since they do not use it to include changed items.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to בית הלל, isn't it written "also"?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בית הלל. The Torah wrote the word "גם", so what do they learn from it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי use "גם" to include a changed item in the איסור. בית הלל do not accept that rule, so the word seems to have no job. That leaves them looking like they ignore a word in the Torah.

keyTerms.meaning: "Also": a word that usually adds something extra
But it is written!

phrases.english: And בית הלל, isn't it written "also"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges בית הלל's reading from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's reading of the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Every word in the Torah should teach something. "גם" seems to have no use for בית הלל.

steps.title: "גם" stays a difficulty for בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it has no answer: the word "גם" is difficult for בית הלל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא does not answer the question. It admits the word "גם" remains a problem for בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "קשיא" here means the question is left standing. This does not mean בית הלל's view is thrown out. It is just an open difficulty.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; the question is left unanswered

steps.confusionAlert: "קשיא" is not the same as "תיובתא". A קשיא is an unanswered question, but the view still stands. A תיובתא knocks the view down.

phrases.english: "Also" is difficult for בית הלל.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from step 3 without answering it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The question on בית הלל from "גם" remains open, but their view is not rejected.

steps.title: The argument is only about ownership, not about payment
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי and בית הלל argue only about whether שינוי קונה. Everyone agrees that the thief pays כפל and ארבעה וחמשה based on the item as it was when he stole it.
steps.simpleTranslation: They only argue about this: one holds that a change acquires, and one holds that a change does not acquire. But about payment, everyone agrees he pays based on the original state, as it teaches: he pays double payment and four- and five-fold payment according to what he stole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets the limits of the argument. The מחלוקת is only about who owns the changed item. On how much the thief pays, both sides agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל hold שינוי קונה, so the thief owns the changed item. בית שמאי hold אין שינוי קונה. Even so, the ברייתא shows that the fines are always figured by the item as it was at the time of the theft.

keyTerms.meaning: A change in an item gives the thief ownership of it
Double payment that a thief pays
Four or five times the value, paid for stealing and then slaughtering or selling a sheep or an ox
Like what he stole: based on its state at the time of the theft
As it was at the start

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת about שינוי קונה is about ownership. The fines are paid according to what was stolen, in everyone's view.

phrases.english: They only disagree here,
in that one master holds: a change acquires,
phrases.notes: This "master" is בית הלל, who permit a changed אתנן.

phrases.english: and the other master holds: a change does not acquire;
but regarding payment,
everyone agrees he pays according to the original state,
as it teaches: he pays double payment
phrases.notes: This is the ברייתא quoted earlier on the daf, about lambs that grew into rams.

phrases.english: and four- and five-fold payment according to what he stole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the פסוק back to the practical rule, and limits the מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת is only about whether שינוי קונה. Everyone agrees that כפל and ארבעה וחמשה are paid based on the original state of the item.

steps.title: Does this ברייתא refute רב?
steps.stepSummary: רב said the fines are paid by the value at the time of trial. This seems to clash with the ברייתא, which says they are paid according to what was stolen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב? For רב said: the principal is paid according to what he stole, but double payment and four- and five-fold payment are paid according to the time of standing in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the ברייתא from the last step to attack רב's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב splits the payments: the קרן is figured by the time of the theft, but the fines by the time of the trial. The ברייתא says the fines are figured by the item as it was stolen. These look like a direct contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation that knocks down a view
The principal: the basic value of the stolen item
The time when the case is brought to court
Shall we say?

phrases.english: Shall we say this is a refutation of רב,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב: קֶרֶן – כְּעֵין שֶׁגָּנַב מְשַׁלֵּם,
phrases.english: for רב said: the principal he pays according to what he stole,
double payment and four- and five-fold payment
according to the time of standing in court?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא quoted in step 5 against רב.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the fines are valued at the time of trial
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא values the fines by the item as it was stolen, which seems to contradict רב.

steps.title: רבא: a change in the animal versus a change in its price
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that the ברייתא is about a physical change in the animal, while רב is talking about a change in market price.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: for lambs, he pays as at the start; for value, he pays as it is now.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא saves רב from the refutation. He shows that the ברייתא and רב are talking about two different kinds of change.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the animal itself changed (a lamb grew into a ram), the fines follow its original state, as the ברייתא says. If only its market price changed, the fines follow today's price at the trial, as רב says. So there is no contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: Lambs
Value or price
As it is now

steps.whatToRemember: A physical change is measured from the time of the theft. A change in price is measured at the time of trial.

phrases.english: רבא said: lambs, as at the start;
phrases.notes: He means lambs that grew into rams after being stolen: pay as they were when taken.

phrases.english: value, as of now.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge on רב from step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases: a physical change versus a change in market price
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if the ברייתא and רב contradict each other about valuing the fines.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about the animal's physical state. רב is about a change in its price.

steps.title: רבה: שינוי קונה is both in the Torah and in a משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבה announces that the rule שינוי קונה has a source in a פסוק and also in a משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: a change acquires; it is written, and we learned it.
steps.whatsHappening: A new section starts. רבה states that שינוי קונה has two sources, and this line sets up the proofs that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, שינוי קונה was presented as בית הלל's view in a מחלוקת. רבה now says it is grounded in the Torah itself and in a משנה. The next step brings the first source.

keyTerms.meaning: It is written in the Torah

phrases.english: רבה said: a change acquires;
it is written, and we learned it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה: שִׁינּוּי קוֹנֶה – כְּתִיבָא וּתְנֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section that looks for sources for שינוי קונה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שינוי קונה has a source in the Torah and in a משנה.

steps.title: The proof from the פסוק "אשר גזל"
steps.stepSummary: The extra words "אשר גזל" teach that the robber returns the item only if it is still as it was when he robbed it. Otherwise he pays money.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: "He shall return the stolen item that he robbed." Why does the verse say "that he robbed"? If it is like what he robbed, he returns it; and if not, he only needs to pay money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings his first source, from the Torah. He learns from words in the פסוק that seem extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "אשר גזל" seems unnecessary, so it must be teaching something. It limits returning the item itself to when it is unchanged. Once it has changed, the robber owns it and pays its value instead, and this is שינוי קונה.

keyTerms.meaning: "He shall return the stolen item"
Why does the verse need to say this?
He returns it
Just money

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the Torah source for the basic rule in robbery that a changed item belongs to the robber, who owes its value.
steps.whatToRemember: An unchanged item goes back to the owner. A changed item stays with the robber, and he pays money.

phrases.english: It is written:
"He shall return the stolen item that he robbed,"
why does the verse say "that he robbed"?
If it is like what he robbed, he returns it;
and if not,
he only needs to pay money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first source that רבה promised in step 8.

steps.title: Proof from a משנה about wood made into vessels
steps.stepSummary: רבה brings the משנה source he promised: a robber who turns wood into vessels, or wool into garments, pays only what the materials were worth when he stole them.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned it in a משנה: Someone who robs wood and makes it into vessels, or wool and makes it into garments, pays what it was worth at the time of the robbery.
steps.whatsHappening: In Step 8, רבה said שינוי קונה has a source in a פסוק and in a משנה. Step 9 gave the פסוק, and now this step gives the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The robber does not have to give back the finished vessels or garments. He only pays the value of the raw wood or wool. That shows the physical change made the item his, which means שינוי קונה.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the value at the time of the robbery
Wood and vessels: raw material versus a finished product

phrases.english: We learned it: one who robs wood
and made it into vessels,
or wool and made it into garments,
pays according to the time of the robbery.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the משנה source that רבה promised in Step 8, after the פסוק source in Step 9.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה of הגוזל עצים ועשאן כלים

steps.title: Another משנה: dyed wool is exempt from the first-shearing gift
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers a different משנה as the source: if a person dyed the first wool shearing before giving it to the כהן, he is exempt. So a change makes it a new item, and שינוי קונה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or another option: If he did not manage to give it to the כהן before he dyed it, he is exempt. So we see that a change acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a second משנה that could also be רבה's source, and then draws the conclusion that שינוי קונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the wool is dyed, the Torah's obligation to give it to the כהן no longer applies, because it now counts as a different item. If a change makes an item 'new' here, then a change also makes a stolen item belong to the thief.

keyTerms.meaning: Or else, another option
The first wool shearing, which is given to a כהן
So we see, this shows
A change in the item makes it belong to the one who changed it

steps.whatToRemember: Both the פסוק (Step 9) and the משניות (Steps 10-11) show that a physical change makes a stolen item belong to the thief. He pays money instead of returning the item.

phrases.aramaic: אִי נָמֵי – לֹא הִסְפִּיק לִיתְּנוֹ לוֹ
phrases.english: Alternatively: if he did not manage to give it to him
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the כהן. This משנה is about ראשית הגז, the first wool shearing that goes to the כהן.

phrases.english: until he dyed it, he is exempt.
So we see that a change acquires.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second משנה as another possible source for the same rule, then states the conclusion.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about ראשית הגז that was dyed

steps.title: Despair also acquires, but is it Torah or rabbinic law?
steps.stepSummary: רבה moves on to יאוש. The חכמים say that the owner's יאוש lets the thief acquire the item, but we do not know whether this is a Torah law or a rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: About יאוש: the חכמים say that it acquires. However, we do not know whether that is from the Torah or from the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה starts a new point. Besides a change in the item, the owner giving up hope also lets the thief acquire it, but the source of this law is unclear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a second way the thief can acquire, separate from שינוי. רבה has no doubt that יאוש works. His only question is whether its force is דאורייתא or דרבנן, and the next lines explain each side. (רב יוסף will disagree in step 15.)

keyTerms.meaning: The owner giving up hope of getting the item back
However
From the Torah
From the חכמים (rabbinic)

steps.confusionAlert: רבה's doubt is not about whether יאוש acquires. He holds that it does. His doubt is only about whether that law comes from the Torah or from the חכמים. רב יוסף, in step 15, says it does not acquire at all.

phrases.english: Despair: the Sages say that it acquires,
phrases.notes: He means the thief acquires the stolen item once the owner gives up hope.

phrases.english: however, we do not know
whether it is by Torah law or by rabbinic law.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from שינוי to a second way of acquiring a stolen item: יאוש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The owner's יאוש lets the thief acquire the item, but whether this is דאורייתא or דרבנן is left open.

steps.title: If it is Torah law, it works like finding a lost item
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains the דאורייתא side. A finder keeps a lost item if the owner gave up hope before it reached the finder's hands. In the same way, the thief acquires once the owner gives up hope.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it is from the Torah, it is just like someone who finds a lost item. Doesn't the finder acquire it once the owner gave up hope before it came into his hands? Here too, once the owner gives up hope, the thief acquires it. So we see that he acquires.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא lays out the reasoning for the first possibility, that יאוש works מדאורייתא, by comparing it to a found lost item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a lost item, the Torah lets the finder keep it if the owner gave up hope before the finder picked it up. On this side, the same principle applies to a thief: the owner's יאוש cuts off his ownership, so the thief acquires. This explains only the דאורייתא side.

keyTerms.meaning: Just like, the same as
One who finds a lost item
Its owner
Acquires

phrases.aramaic: אִי דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא – מִידֵּי דַּהֲוָה אַמּוֹצֵא אֲבֵידָה;
phrases.english: If it is Torah law, it is just like one who finds a lost item;
one who finds a lost item, is it not so that
once its owner has despaired of it
before it came into his hands, he acquires it?
phrases.notes: 'His hands' means the finder's. The owner gave up hope before the finder picked it up.

phrases.english: This one too: once its owner has despaired,
he acquires it. So we see that he acquires.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא – מִידֵּי דַּהֲוָה אַמּוֹצֵא אֲבֵידָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Develops the first side (דאורייתא) of the doubt raised in Step 12.
steps.raayaObject: That יאוש acquires for a thief מדאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: A comparison to מוצא אבידה, where יאוש before the finder takes the item lets him keep it

steps.title: The rabbinic side: a stolen item is not like a lost item
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the comparison to אבידה does not work. A finder got the item in a permitted way, but a thief got it through a sin. So יאוש helps a thief only מדרבנן, because of תקנת השבים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe a stolen item is not like a lost item. With a lost item, the finder got it in a permitted way. But here the thief got it in a forbidden way. So the rule is only from the Rabbis, who said the thief should acquire it as an enactment to help people who repent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side of רבה's question. It pushes away the proof from אבידה and says יאוש helps a thief only because the Rabbis said so.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 compared a thief to a finder. Here the גמרא points out a big difference: the finder did nothing wrong, but the thief took the item through a sin. So the Torah's rule for lost items cannot be copied over to theft. The Rabbis made יאוש work for a thief only so that thieves who want to repent can pay money instead of returning the item itself.

keyTerms.meaning: A lost item
In a permitted way
In a forbidden way, through a sin
From the Rabbis (rabbinic law, not Torah law)
An enactment for people who repent, to make it easier for them to do תשובה

steps.confusionAlert: Even on this side, the thief still owes the owner. תקנת השבים only means he may pay the item's value instead of handing back the item itself.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the two sides of רבה's doubt, דאורייתא or דרבנן, and leads straight into רב יוסף's opinion that יאוש does not work at all.

phrases.english: Or perhaps it is not comparable to a lost item,
phrases.notes: "It" is the stolen item. This answers the comparison the גמרא made in step 13.

phrases.english: for a lost item is something that, when it came into his hand,
came into his hand in a permitted way;
but this one,
phrases.notes: He means the thief and his stolen item.

phrases.english: since it came into his hand in a forbidden way,
it is only from the Rabbis;
for the Rabbis said that he should acquire it,
because of an enactment for those who repent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of רבה's question and pushes away the comparison to אבידה from step 13.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects learning the law of a thief from the law of a lost item.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A finder got the item in a permitted way, but a thief got it through a sin, so the two cases are not alike.
steps.raayaObject: That יאוש helps a thief only מדרבנן

steps.title: רב יוסף: יאוש does not let a thief acquire at all
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף holds that יאוש does not help a thief acquire the item, not even by rabbinic law.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: יאוש does not make the thief the owner, not even from the Rabbis.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף gives his own opinion, which is stricter than both sides of רבה's question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה was unsure whether יאוש works for a thief by Torah law or by rabbinic law, but he agreed it works. רב יוסף says it does not work at all. So even after the owner gives up hope, the stolen item still belongs to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: The owner giving up hope of getting his item back
Does not make someone the owner
And even

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רבה and רב יוסף. רבה says יאוש works (he only asks why). רב יוסף says it does not work at all.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:
Giving up hope does not make him acquire,
and not even by rabbinic law.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יוֹסֵף אָמַר: יֵאוּשׁ אֵינוֹ קוֹנֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבה's two possible reasons, רב יוסף disagrees with the basic rule itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: יאוש does not let a thief acquire a stolen item, not by Torah law and not by rabbinic law.

steps.title: רב יוסף begins a challenge to רבה from a case of stolen חמץ
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף begins to challenge רבה from a משנה about someone who stole חמץ and then פסח passed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף challenged רבה: If someone robbed חמץ and פסח passed over it...
steps.whatsHappening: This line is setting up the next move. רב יוסף starts quoting a משנה to attack רבה, and the rest of the case comes in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here רב יוסף has only given the opening of the case: חמץ was stolen, and then פסח went by. Once פסח passes over חמץ, it becomes forbidden to benefit from. The ruling of the משנה, and how it is used against רבה, come next.

keyTerms.meaning: He robbed
Leavened bread or food
